_notes: Ranges of the ISA instance set. Every batch draws its instances with a Latin hypercube over 'instance',
and pairs each generated instance with 'fleet.draws_per_instance' fleets drawn over 'fleet'.
Edit the ranges here; make_batch.py reads this file for every new batch.
A setting given as [low, high] is drawn; a single number is held fixed (it stays out of the hypercube).
Batch 2: start_hour is fixed. For a static solver with a constant travel-time matrix, shifting all times changes nothing,
so it was a dead axis; the afternoon window also keeps latest arrivals well before midnight (86400 s).
Batch 2: inbound_share (1 = every trip goes from homes to attractions, 0 = the reverse, 0.5 = both ways) and
concentration (0 = uniform over the zones as in batch 1, 2 = demand packed into the densest zones) replace uniform demand;
make_batch.py needs zone_weights.py output for them. Scenario labels a/b/c are derived from inbound_share.
max_dtt_s only rejects long trips: with zone weights the generator ignores the min/max dtt ring around the origin.
Batch 1 used start_hour [12, 19.5], max_dtt_s 3600 and uniform demand (no inbound_share, no concentration).
